stem: A 14-year-old girl had a kidney transplant 6 months ago and needed very strong immunosuppression for rejection. She now has enlarged lymph nodes, liver and spleen. A node biopsy shows sheets of a single type of B cell.
oneliner: 14F + kidney transplant 6 mo + heavy immunosuppression + lymph nodes, liver, spleen enlarged + monomorphic B-cell sheets → what will testing find?
ask: Further study of these B cells will most likely show which of the following?

whyNot.A: Owl's-eye inclusions; causes **retinitis, colitis, pneumonitis**, not a B-cell growth
whyNot.C: Infects **CD4 T cells**; she has no HIV risk

why: **Heavy immunosuppression + growing B cells** = post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. **EBV** infects B cells through **CD21** and drives them to divide when T cells can't control it.
chain: EBV binds CD21 on B cells

bug.name: Epstein-Barr virus (HHV-4)
bug.lab: Heterophile (Monospot) antibodies; atypical CD8 T cells on smear
bug.virulence: Enters B cells via CD21; latency
bug.causes: Mononucleosis; Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, PTLD, hairy leukoplakia
